rules_evaluated.evidence: compound-and-close-1's fence opens 'Review this session end-to-end: the orientation and introspection, the /context read, the TDD bug fix, the diff push-back.' Three of the four referents check out via the registry's requires/produces graph (orient-and-introspect-2's introspection turn, fix-tests-first-3's TDD fix, and the free-form diff-pushback turn from fix-tests-first.md's body-only pushback move — all genuine prior turns in the same session's scrollback). The fourth, 'the /context read', is the literal content of prompt orient-and-introspect-3, which is just the slash command '/context'. WebFetch of code.claude.com/docs/en/commands (2026-07-11) indicates /context is a client-side visualization command ('Visualize current context usage as a colored grid') with no documented signal that its invocation or output is logged into the model-visible conversation — i.e. Claude reviewing 'this session end-to-end' later may have no actual memory of that turn. Docs-derived, not live-tested (per check_platform_and_boundaries.md #5a, docs are lower-confidence for runtime behavior than a live probe) — flagged as live-probe-owed, not asserted as certain fact. Low practical impact: it's one clause in a four-item recap list, and the other three referents give Claude ample real material to write the rules file from.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Live-probe: in a real session, type /context, then ask a later turn what it showed. If confirmed invisible to the model, either drop '/context read' from the recap clause or have the student explicitly narrate the reading back to Claude in chat so it lands in scrollback.
